supplement_for.base_course_title: CS294/194-280: Advanced Large Language Model Agents
supplement_for.relationship: Use the Stanford official course overview and schedule to extend the Spring 2025 Berkeley textbook on self-improvement, tool use, planning, coding agents, evaluation, research automation, memory, and robotics.

source_of_truth.notes: Only official Stanford course-site pages are used as canonical sources. No official public video page or official slide page was found on the site.

course_level_sources.notes: Primary source for course overview, staff, logistics, grading, and project structure.
Primary source for session ordering, dates, topic labels, and official reading links.

excluded_or_noncanonical_sources_conside.notes: Mentioned only as an instructor-affiliated public lead. Not treated as canonical because the official Stanford course site does not publish it as the course video source-of-truth, and the playlist labeling does not cleanly match the Autumn 2025 official schedule.

missing_or_uncertain_sources.note: No official public video page or official playlist link was found on the Stanford course site.
No official public slide page or per-lecture slide index was found on the Stanford course site.
Because lecture recordings and slides were not published on the official site, this supplement reconstructs the course only at the official schedule/readings level, not as full lecture transcripts.

logistics.research_emphasis: The official page states that students learn from latest research papers, discuss suggested readings, work on an original research project, and learn from invited academic and industry speakers.

sessions.title: Course Overview
sessions.notes: Defines the self-improving AI agents framing used by the supplement.

sessions.title: Test-time Compute Scaling
readings: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling (Brown et al. 2024)
Archon: An Architecture Search Framework for Inference-Time Techniques (Saad-Falcon et al. 2024)
Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters (Snell et al. 2024)
How Do Large Language Monkeys Get Their Power (Laws)?
sessions.notes: Pushes the Berkeley Spring 2025 reasoning discussion toward explicit scaling-law and architecture-search framing.

sessions.title: Robust Verification
readings: Shrinking the Generation-Verification Gap with Weak Verifiers
Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems (Cobbe et al. 2021)
Let's Verify Step by Step (Lightman et al. 2023)
Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations (Wang et al. 2023)
sessions.notes: Moves verification earlier in the curriculum and makes weak verifiers a central design object.

sessions.title: Learning from feedback with tools/code
readings: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al. 2022)
RLEF: Grounding Code LLMs in Execution Feedback with Reinforcement Learning
Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
sessions.notes: Connects tools, code execution, and feedback-learning in one self-improvement loop.

sessions.title: Multi-step Reasoning/Planning
readings: SWiRL: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models (Zhou et al. 2023)
SPRINT: Enabling Interleaved Planning and Parallelized Execution in Reasoning Models
ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models (Prasad et al. 2024)
Wider or Deeper? Scaling LLM Inference-Time Compute with Adaptive Branching Tree Search
sessions.notes: Builds a planning-heavy continuation of the Berkeley memory-and-planning chapter.

sessions.title: Train Time Scaling/Scaling RL
readings: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning (Zelikman et al. 2022)
DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
sessions.notes: Sharpens the train-time self-improvement side of the Spring 2025 textbook.

sessions.title: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
readings: Automated design of agentic systems
The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery (Lu et al. 2024)
AlphaEvolve: A Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms
sessions.notes: Makes open-ended discovery and agent-system design explicit curricular targets.

sessions.title: Self improvement with Search & Deep Research Agents
readings: Competition-Level Code Generation with AlphaCode
AlphaCode 2 Technical Report
Search-o1: Agentic Search-Enhanced Large Reasoning Models
sessions.notes: Bridges competitive code generation, search, and deep-research style agents.
